data.narrative:
Longshot Space is a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Mike Grace and Nathan Saichek, having raised $10M+ to date. The target operates within a sector spanning 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Rocket Lab, SpaceX, and ICEYE.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. Stage-progression anchoring, using total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression in venture capital. This method yields an implied valuation of $25M. The peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in the Space & Aerospace sector (only one same-stage peer identified against a minimum threshold of three required datapoints). Public-comp anchoring via revenue multiples was similarly inapplicable, as private company revenue data remains undisclosed; while the sector median P/S stands at 24.4x across the five public tickers, without Longshot Space's revenue on file, meaningful calibration is impossible.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $21M–$29M, with a median of $25M. This range carries material uncertainty given the single-method foundation. Key dependencies include validation of the 2.5x step-up assumption for this specific company and sector, as well as obtaining revenue or revenue-proxy metrics that would enable public-comp anchoring. Additional private-stage comparables at identical or adjacent maturity levels would strengthen conviction.
